Here are the main South Korea stories from mid-October 2026, based on the search results.

**Inter-Korean tensions and the DMZ**
- Seoul is pressing Pyongyang over a September 21 landmine blast in the DMZ that wounded South Korean soldiers. A landmine explosion injured three South Korean soldiers in the Korean Demilitarized Zone, and Seoul demands an apology while North Korea denies planting mines.
- President Lee Jae Myung's government is treating the incident as a possible opening for talks. The Lee administration and the Ministry of Unification are trying to use the DMZ incident to support inter-Korean dialogue and sustain a "peaceful coexistence" policy.
- Missile activity continues. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said a ballistic missile fired from Wonsan flew more than 700 kilometres. Another report says one of the missiles launched from the Pyongyang area flew more than 900km. Also, North Korea says it tested a new torpedo with AI technology.

**Diplomacy with Ukraine**
- South Korea announced it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine, after President Lee threatened punitive steps if Ukraine refused to apologize over the revelation about North Korean prisoners of war.

**Economy and markets**
- South Korea is betting on Egypt as an export hub despite rising financial risks.
- A Korea Pro report noted a five-day KOSPI sell-off, which raises questions about whether chip profits will last. (The source describes this as a stock rout that exposes fiscal risks as investors question future semiconductor profits despite record earnings.)
- The won is also under pressure. With WGBI entry ending in November, pension fund swaps and Washington's investment demands loom over currency policy.
- On trade with the US, Seoul says it will only invest in commercially viable projects, following a package that includes nuclear plants and Texas power generation.

**Domestic politics**
- A cabinet nomination dispute is in the news. A feature traces how past presidents responded to nomination disputes, from Lee Myung-bak's questionnaires to the latest reshuffle.

**Crime and society**
- A shopping centre stabbing in Incheon left eight people injured. The Justice Ministry has apologised after the suspect met his probation officer hours before the attack.
- Several Korean dramas are airing or premiering this month, including Doctor X: Mafia in White on SBS TV, and Final Table on JTBC, scheduled for October 24.

**Note on dates:** Some of the search results show inconsistent "age" labels (for example, one October 2026 article is labelled as 639 days old), so the publication dates in the article text are more reliable than those labels. For the latest developments, check the source sites directly, since this is a snapshot from search results and not a live feed.

이번 검색에서는 2026년 10월 중순(12~18일) 국내 뉴스가 가장 많이 잡혔습니다. 한 주간 흐름을 기준으로 정리하면 다음과 같습니다.

**1. 증시 급락과 반도체 불안**
- 한 주간 리뷰에 따르면 반도체와 AI 기대감이 불안으로 바뀌면서 주가가 급락했습니다. 13일 코스피는 5.5% 급락하며 장중 6,000선이 무너졌고, 이틀 뒤인 15일에는 반도체주 중심의 매도세가 확산해 시장 전체 거래를 일시 중단하는 서킷브레이커가 발동됐다.
- 원인으로는 대규모 데이터센터와 반도체 설비에 투입되는 자금이 수익으로 얼마나 빨리 회수될 수 있는지에 대한 우려가 꼽혔습니다.
- 반면 정부 측은 낙관적입니다. 이형일 부총리는 "반도체 호황이 내년까지 이어지고 수요가 공급을 웃돈다"고 언급했고, 3대 신용평가사는 반도체·AI 호황이 한국 성장 둔화 우려를 상쇄한다고 평가했습니다.
- 시장 분위기는 원·달러 NDF가 3.95원 상승하고 미 30년 금리가 5.6%를 넘어서는 등 환율·금리 부담도 함께 보여줬습니다.

**2. 대외 관계와 안보**
- 국제사회에서는 중동 전쟁을 둘러싼 한국의 군사적 역할이 다시 논쟁의 대상이 됐다.
- 북한 관련해서는 압록강에서 나타난 변화가 외교적 선언보다 구체적이었는데, 사람과 물자가 이동할 수 있는 통로가 실제로 열린 것이라는 분석이 나왔습니다. 남북 간 군사적 긴장은 이어지고 있습니다.
- 트럼프 미국 대통령의 발언도 주목을 받았습니다. SBS 뉴스 편성표에는 "한국이 500억 달러 투자"라는 트럼프 대통령의 선거전 발언 관련 보도가 있었습니다.

**3. 사회·치안**
- 인천의 한 복합상가에서는 전자발찌를 착용한 남성이 흉기를 휘둘러 여러 시민이 다쳤다.
- 법 개정으로는 개정 형사소송법이 10월 2일부터 시행됐고, 전북경찰청은 수사인력 52명을 보강했다.

**4. 정치**
- 6월 3일 치러진 재보궐선거는 14개 국회의원 지역구 공석으로 치러져 민주화 이후 가장 대규모의 재보궐선거로, 정치적으로 중요하게 여겨졌다.
- 국정감사도 이어지고 있습니다. 인천 지역 국회의원들이 국정감사에서 인천 현안의 해법을 끌어낼지 관심이 쏠렸습니다.

**5. 스포츠**
- 프로야구 포스트시즌에서는 KIA 네일·김도영 선수가 준플레이오프 1차전 승리를 합작했다는 소식이 있었습니다.

**참고 사항**
- 검색 결과가 주로 10월 중순 이전의 주간 리뷰와 뉴스 목록 페이지여서, 10월 한 달 전체를 아우르는 자료는 충분하지 않았습니다. 특정 사안을 더 자세히 알고 싶으면 알려주세요.

Links: [{"title":"mbiz.heraldcorp.com","url":"https://mbiz.heraldcorp.com/article/10903776"},{"title":"news 0195263e78a5","url":"https://stockhub.kr/en/news/news_0195263e78a5"},{"title":"5 of 11 all-time circuit breakers triggered in 2026 alone","url":"https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10789477"},{"title":"kospi circuit breaker heavy selloff cmriu1lwj3arxnw0jxp6y89gt","url":"https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/kospi-circuit-breaker-heavy-selloff-cmriu1lwj3arxnw0jxp6y89gt"},{"title":"my timesThe Korea Times","url":"https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/20260729/bourse-operator-issues-circuit-breaker-for-kospi-on-sharp-fall"},{"title":"-Circuit breaker triggered 3 minutes after open; Kosdaq sell-side sidecar also activated","url":"https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10777811"},{"title":"china markets rise on ai optimism tech stocks surge","url":"https://askfuzz.ai/discover/news/global/china-markets-rise-on-ai-optimism-tech-stocks-surge"},{"title":"Kospi tumbles nearly 10% following massive tech sell-offs","url":"https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/kospi-tumbles-nearly-10-following-massive-tech-selloffs/12737002"},{"title":"Kospi tumbles nearly 10% following massive tech sell-offs","url":"https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/kospi-crashes-999percent-in-historic-tech-rout/12737002"}]

Coverage of the October 15, 2026 sell-off reports a sharp drop and a circuit breaker, but the sources disagree on some details, especially the index levels and the running count of halts.

**What the sources agree on**
- A Korea Times-style report from Herald (dated Oct. 15, 2026) says both indices fell more than 8%, which set off back-to-back circuit breakers. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix fell roughly 10%, and advances by a Chinese chipmaker weighed on semiconductor leaders.
- A separate Etoday report says the KOSPI closed down 8.06%, and the Level 1 halt lasted 20 minutes. It describes this as the first time in about two and a half months since July 29 that a Level 1 breaker had been triggered.
- Foreign investors were the main sellers. In the Etoday data, foreign investors net sold 3.971 trillion won on the KOSPI.
- The Kosdaq also halted. A circuit breaker was triggered on the Kosdaq at 12:23 p.m., suspending all trading for 20 minutes.

**Where the sources conflict**
- **KOSPI level:** The Etoday report puts the close at 5,524.53. Other Herald and Multibagg pieces describe KOSPI levels near 7,400–8,200 during similar sell-offs, though those reports are dated to other sessions. I could not reconcile the levels, so treat the exact index figures as unconfirmed.
- **Count of halts this year:** The Oct. 15 Herald article calls this the 10th time this year a circuit breaker has been activated on the Kospi. Etoday's "first in about two and a half months" framing suggests a different count, and Korea Times reported a July 29 halt as the eighth time this year. These counts can't all be right.
- **Timing:** The Etoday piece is time-stamped 1:53 p.m. KST. The Herald report gives 12:23 p.m. for the Kosdaq halt. These are not necessarily contradictory, but the exact halt times were not consistent across sources.

I ran one search, so I did not check the KRX's official notices. For the official index close, halt times, and the year-to-date halt count, check Korea Exchange's releases directly.

The Justice Ministry apologised after a 59-year-old man wearing an electronic ankle monitor attacked shoppers at a mall in Incheon on Tuesday, 13 October 2026.

**The apology and investigation:** The ministry said "We deeply apologise for causing great concern to the public over today's knife attack in Incheon involving an individual subject to electronic monitoring," it said in a statement. It also committed to a probe of the case. The ministry acknowledged that the monitoring system failed to prevent the attack and pledged a detailed investigation into his supervision, treatment and risk assessment, and a review of electronic monitoring and parole management. It said it would review both the supervision of the suspect and broader electronic monitoring procedures.

**The suspect's background:** He was sentenced to four years in prison for attempted murder in 2015, according to Yonhap news agency. He was placed under electronic monitoring in 2019 and had committed no repeat offenses while under supervision, the Justice Ministry said. However, he was booked last month on suspicion of carrying a weapon after using a kitchen knife to puncture a protest sign outside a hospital where he had a dispute. The ministry also said authorities detected no attempts to destroy his monitoring device.

**Before the attack:** He attended a counselling session from 10am to 11am and then met his probation officer from 11.20am to 11.55am, the ministry said. The attack began at 1.40pm.

**The attack and casualties:** CCTV footage showed the man running through a room with weapons strapped to both hands, and more than 10 knives were found in his bag. An Incheon Fire Department official said one woman in her twenties was in cardiac arrest and seven other people had been injured. She underwent emergency surgery but had not regained consciousness. Shoppers and staff stopped him: the attack ended when he was apprehended by staff and customers who used trays and chairs to defend themselves.

**Government response:** President Lee Jae-myung, visiting an Incheon police agency, demanded a swift and thorough investigation and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

Sources differ slightly on some details. Most reports give eight victims, but the fire department's account cites one critically injured person and seven others hurt, which is the same total. One report also notes that he had previously been punished for breaching restrictions on leaving his home while wearing the device. The Justice Ministry's statement, by contrast, says there was no breach connected with the attack. The ministry has not yet published its investigation findings in these results.

2. **Incheon mall stabbing:** On October 13 a 59-year-old man wearing an electronic ankle monitor stabbed eight people at an Incheon shopping complex, and the Justice Ministry apologised because he had met his probation officer only hours before. — [SCMP](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3370755/south-korea-shopping-centre-stabbing-leaves-8-injured)

3. **North Korean weapons test:** North Korean state media said on October 17 that the North had tested a new high-speed torpedo that uses AI to find and guide toward targets, shortly after testing submarine-launched cruise missiles, raising tension on the peninsula. — [The Star (Reuters/KCNA)](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/10/17/north-korea-tests-new-ai-equipped-torpedo-kcna-says)

Sources disagree on some details, including the exact KOSPI close and how many circuit breakers have been triggered this year. The torpedo claims come only from North Korean state media and haven't been independently confirmed. The pick for the third story is a judgement call: if you'd rather have a domestic one, President Lee Jae-myung's approval rating recovered after two weeks of decline. South Korea's recall of its ambassador to Ukraine (October 8) was a major story but falls just outside the 7-day window.
